name: Vapi
category: Developer platform for voice AI agents
positioning: A developer-focused platform for building and running voice agents, where you choose the transcription, language model and voice providers yourself.

pricing.model: A per-minute platform fee, with transcription, language model, voice and telephony providers billed separately
pricing.headline: A platform fee of $0.05 per minute, plus provider charges for each component
planNotes: The pricing page lists Free, Core, Pro and Premier tiers.
The Pro tier lists a monthly minimum on the pricing page.

strengths.claim: Lets you pick the transcription, language model and voice providers, which gives developers control over each part of a call.
Documents support for connecting your own SIP trunk as well as Twilio and Telnyx numbers.
Documents an MCP integration so agents can call tools and external clients can manage assistants.

limitations.claim: The total cost per minute depends on which providers you choose, so it cannot be read from a single price.
The documentation describes assistants through configuration; we did not find a visual flow canvas described.

compliance.note: The trust center lists SOC 2 reports, and the pricing page describes HIPAA as a paid add-on.

migration.exportAgentsPossible: Assistant configuration can be read through the API.
stepsToLeave: List your assistants through the Vapi API and save each assistant's configuration, prompt and tool list.
Download the recordings and transcripts for the calls you need to keep.
Note which phone numbers you imported from your own carrier and which you bought through Vapi.
Cancel the plan once calls have moved.

bestFor: Developers who want to assemble their own voice stack and manage each provider.
